reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch treat Judah's burning of Jerusalem as real but temporary, since the Jebusites soon retook and rebuilt the city before the later notice in Judges 1:21.

discrepancy.note: Paine argues the Judges 1:8 capture notice cannot be squared with the parallel Jebusites-in-Jerusalem 'unto this day' report he traces to Joshua 15:63.

quotes.text: "Now the children of Judah had fought against Jerusalem, and taken it;" consequently this book could not have been written before Jerusalem had been taken. … The reader will recollect the quotation I have just before made from Joshua xv. 63, where it said that the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem at this day
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Judges 1:8.

sides.snippet: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
sides.verseText: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

sides.snippet: The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
sides.verseText: The children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
